trend_source: A woman was arrested Aug 6 in Singapore's 'Fun Coffee' Ponzi scheme investigation - a crypto-linked MLM app that promised outsized returns and left victims across Singapore, Hong Kong and Macau unable to withdraw funds.
title: The 'Fun Coffee' Ponzi bust is your permission slip to ask 'wait, how does this actually make money?'
why_it_works: It's a live, local cautionary tale people are already discussing - showing the anatomy of a scam (recruit friends, promised returns, can't withdraw) makes the red flags concrete instead of abstract, without shaming anyone who got caught out.
hooks: You've probably seen the 'Fun Coffee' scam headlines this week - here's the one question that would've stopped it cold.
A coffee app promised 'unrealistically high returns' and recruitment bonuses - sound familiar? Let's break down why that's the tell.
An app that sold coffee and 'investment plans' just got busted in Singapore - here's how to spot the next one before it's you.
talking_points: The red flag: any plan that pays you MORE for recruiting other people than for the product itself is a pyramid, not an investment.
'Unrealistically high, guaranteed returns' is the tell - real investments carry real risk, and nobody can promise you a fixed high payout.
Before moving money anywhere, check if the platform or person is actually licensed - MAS keeps a public register you can search in two minutes.
If you can't withdraw your own money on demand, that's not a delay, that's the scheme telling you something.
cta: Not sure if something you've been offered is legit? DM me 'CHECK' and I'll walk through it with you, no judgment.
how_to_film: Talking head, phone in hand as if scrolling the news. Hold up phone to camera briefly on the 'sound familiar?' line. Text overlay listing the 3 red flags one at a time as you say them.

trend_source: US markets had a big rebound week - the Dow and S&P touched record highs and the Nasdaq jumped over 5% as a weak jobs report fed hopes of a Fed rate cut, with AI stocks leading the charge.
title: AI stocks just had their best week in months - here's the conversation to have before you FOMO in
why_it_works: A dramatic green week triggers real FOMO, especially among clients who feel like they're missing out - naming that feeling openly, without recommending any stock, builds trust instead of hype.
hooks: AI stocks just ripped higher this week and I've had three people ask if they've 'missed the boat' - let's talk about that feeling.
The Nasdaq just had one of its best weeks in months. Here's the question worth asking before you chase it.
A record-high week in the market always brings the same DM: 'should I put more in now?' Here's my honest answer.
talking_points: A strong week doesn't tell you anything about next week - markets that are up can keep going up or reverse fast.
FOMO is a normal, human reaction to seeing green everywhere - the goal isn't to suppress it, it's to not act on it alone.
The real question isn't 'is this the right entry point,' it's 'does my current plan already account for weeks like this happening sometimes.'
If your portfolio matches your actual time horizon and risk comfort, a rally week changes nothing about what you should do.
cta: If a week like this has you second-guessing your plan, drop a comment 'PLAN' and I'll reach out.

trend_source: The Straits Times Index closed its ninth straight week of gains in the first week of August, ending around 5,698 points, driven by strong bank earnings.
title: The STI just posted its ninth straight winning week - here's the boring, correct response
why_it_works: A 9-week streak feels significant and prompts 'should I get in now' questions - reframing a hot streak as a reason to check your plan rather than chase performance protects clients from performance-chasing, the single most common investing mistake.
hooks: The STI just closed its ninth straight week of gains. Before you get excited, here's what that number actually means.
Nine weeks of gains in a row on our home index - feels good, but here's the trap that number sets.
Everyone's talking about the STI's winning streak this week - here's the one thing streaks never tell you.
talking_points: Nine consecutive up-weeks is unusual, and unusual runs make people want to add money right at the top - that's performance chasing.
A streak says nothing about what happens next - the same conditions that produced 9 green weeks could produce a red one just as easily.
The better question: is your current allocation still the one you'd choose if you were starting from scratch today?
Rebalancing back to your target, not adding extra on a high, is usually the move that ages well.
cta: Curious whether your allocation still makes sense after this run? Save this and message me 'REVIEW.'
how_to_film: Carousel: slide 1 the '9 weeks' stat as a bold headline, slide 2 a simple rising-line graphic, slide 3 'what a streak doesn't tell you', slide 4 the rebalancing question, slide 5 CTA.
